headline: SILVER SETTLES $48.65 — ONE-YEAR LOW: Gold Holds $3,888, Ratio Hits 78.7 on Week's Worst Drop
snippet: COMEX silver futures settled at $48.65 on Friday November 13 — down 2.6% on the session and at their lowest level since November 2025 — while gold edged up 0.1% to $3,888 and the gold-silver ratio stretched to approximately 78.7. Silver's weekly decline of roughly 10% outpaced gold's 4.6% five-session fall, extending the correction from January 2026's high above $113 to a drawdown of approximately 57% from peak. For junior silver producers and silver royalty names on the TSX-V and ASX, sustained silver underperformance is compressing the revenue line faster than operating cost reductions can offset — making the ratio's trajectory as important as the gold price itself in the near term.

headline: IS $3,800 THE GOLD FLOOR? CPM Group Sets Support Zones; SILVER BEARS EYE $45-48 on Deeper Fed Slide
snippet: CPM Group has identified a potential support band of $3,800–$3,900 for gold and $45–$48 for silver as the market reprices for an 85% December Fed rate-hike probability — with $3,870 described as the line separating an orderly correction from a deeper structural downtrend. The gold-silver ratio at 78.7 is approaching territory that has historically preceded sharp silver outperformance once monetary policy reverses, but the timing risk is acute: silver's technical signals remain weak and CPM's $45–$48 downside scenario represents a further 7–9% decline from Friday's one-year low close. The analysis frames $3,800 gold as the actionable test level to watch next week.

headline: 30-DAY ROUT: GOLD -5.15%, SILVER -9.97%, COPPER -6.96% — URANIUM LONE BRIGHT SPOT AT +0.61%
snippet: A 30-day commodity performance review dated November 13 shows gold at $3,894 (-5.15%), silver at $50.05 (-9.97%), copper at $6.15/lb (-6.96%), and lithium retreating sharply — while uranium at $90.55/lb was essentially flat (+0.61%), the standout performer across the entire basket. Nickel also held firmer. The divergence between uranium and precious/base metals over the 30-day period underscores how uranium prices are driven primarily by long-term utility contracting rather than short-term macro flows — reinforcing the thesis that uranium offers portfolio diversification from the macro risk-off narrative currently punishing gold and copper.

headline: BUNKER HILL CLOSES SILVER47 MERGER — 388M OZ SILVER-EQUIVALENT INVENTORY, COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION TARGET YEAR-END
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining closed its acquisition of Silver47 Exploration on November 6, creating a 'Made in America' U.S. silver and critical minerals producer with approximately 388 million silver-equivalent ounces across the historic Bunker Hill mine in Idaho and Silver47's portfolio — branding the combined entity as the largest U.S.-focused silver producer by resource inventory. The deal closed via a BC court-approved plan of arrangement and the combined company remains TSX-listed, targeting commercial production at Bunker Hill by year-end 2026. With COMEX silver at a one-year low, the timing places the newly merged company under pressure to demonstrate production execution before the balance sheet begins to strain.

headline: ALTIUS MINERALS BIDS $122M FOR TNR GOLD — 0.4% NSR on McEwen's LOS AZULES Copper; Board Fight Complicates Close
snippet: Altius Minerals has made a bid to acquire the remaining shares of TNR Gold in a deal valued at approximately $122 million, seeking to consolidate 100% ownership of TNR's royalty portfolio — most importantly a 0.4% net smelter return royalty on McEwen Copper's Los Azules porphyry copper project in Argentina, which Rio Tinto and Stellantis have already invested in and which is targeting a construction decision in 2027. The deal has been complicated by a board dispute at TNR. For royalty-focused investors, the transaction signals that Altius believes the Los Azules royalty is worth locking in at current copper prices ahead of a potential construction greenlight that would transform it into a material long-term cash flow stream.

headline: TECK'S HIGHLAND VALLEY COPPER STRIKE ENTERS 3RD WEEK — 1,200 USW Workers Out, Moly Guidance at Risk
snippet: United Steelworkers Local 7619's strike at Teck Resources' Highland Valley Copper mine in British Columbia — Canada's largest open-pit copper mine — has entered its third week with no resolution announced, as 1,200+ workers remain on the picket line following the collapse of contract talks over wages and pensions. Teck's 2026 molybdenum production guidance for Highland Valley sits at 1,500–1,800 tonnes against approximately 700 tonnes in H1, meaning a prolonged shutdown increasingly risks missing the full-year target. For junior copper explorers watching macro conditions, an extended supply outage at a Tier-1 Canadian mine arriving simultaneously with SHFE copper inventories at three-year lows is a physical tightness data point the futures market has been discounting.

headline: ANFIELD DRILLS 8 WELLS, TARGETS 1,000 tpd UTAH MILL UPGRADE — Shootaring Canyon License Decision Expected Q4
snippet: Anfield Energy (TSXV: AEC) has completed 8 exploration wells at its Utah operations and begun engineering work on the 1,000 tonnes-per-day throughput upgrade at its Shootaring Canyon uranium mill — North America's only fully licensed conventional uranium mill not currently in production — while awaiting final renewal of its radioactive materials license from Utah state regulators, expected by year-end 2026. The company's Velvet-Wood underground mine, the first energy project approved under Trump's accelerated 14-day permitting process in early 2026, is expected to feed Shootaring Canyon. If licensed on schedule, Anfield adds a second conventional U.S. uranium mill to the domestic production chain at $90/lb uranium, closing a supply gap federal agencies have identified as a national security issue.

headline: INTEGRA RESOURCES CUTS FLORIDA CANYON GUIDANCE 15% — AISC Hits $3,300-3,500/oz as Heap Leach Rates Disappoint
snippet: Integra Resources (TSX: ITR) cut its 2026 gold production guidance for the Florida Canyon heap leach mine in Nevada to 59,000–62,000 ounces from 70,000–75,000 in its Q3 results — a 15% reduction — as slower-than-expected leach rates have delayed recovery of ounces already stacked on the pads. Mine-site all-in sustaining costs are now guided at $3,300–$3,500 per ounce, well above the original $2,750–$2,950. Management says higher-grade Central Pit ore is on track for 2027. The miss is a reminder that heap leach operations carry specific metallurgical risks distinct from macro drivers — and that AISC creep above $3,000/oz is becoming a sector-wide accountability issue as gold corrects from its $4,000+ highs.

headline: SILVER AT ONE-YEAR LOW: BEAR TRAP OR LONGER SLIDE? — The Case For and Against $45 Silver from Here
snippet: With COMEX silver at a one-year low of $48.65, the two competing interpretations: the bear trap case (ratio at 78.7 is at a historically mean-reverting extreme; physical demand has not collapsed; a Fed pivot in H1 2027 would trigger a sharp silver recovery) versus the continuation case (silver technically weak, ratio can expand toward 85+ in prior rate-tightening cycles, and the January 2026 high above $113 was a speculative overshoot still being unwound). The analysis identifies $45–$48 as the CPM-modelled support band and argues investors deploying new capital into silver here should use staged entries across the range rather than a single commitment.

headline: WHY JUNIOR MINERS FALL 30-40% WHILE GOLD FALLS 20% — Leverage Math That Crushes Retail Portfolios in Corrections
snippet: Discovery Alert maps the mathematics of mining stock leverage in a correcting gold market: when gold falls 20–25% from peak, junior miners (GDXJ) have historically fallen 30–40% due to operating leverage on narrowing margins, valuation multiple compression as growth narratives reprice, and retail stop-loss selling that creates liquidity gaps in small-cap names. The piece argues that the current correction has already stress-tested many juniors' cash runways, and companies with less than 18 months of cash on hand are approaching forced capital raise territory — at a time when equity markets for junior miners are effectively closed. The leverage that amplifies gains in a bull market operates identically in reverse.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER CORRECTION: IS THE BOTTOM NEAR? — Historical Selloff Map Sets $3,800 as the Line in the Sand
snippet: Gold Survival Guide maps the current drawdown against prior gold bull market corrections — 2006, 2008, 2012, and 2021 — and identifies $3,800 gold as the zone where, in prior cycles, corrections of this duration and velocity have tended to find buyers. Very few gold miners currently trade above their 200-day moving averages, a sentiment extreme that in prior corrections preceded 20–30% recovery rallies within 60–90 days. For self-directed investors deciding when to add, the analysis offers a framework: staged buying in the $3,800–$3,900 band with a medium-term target of $4,500–$4,700 for gold, and proportional upside in silver if the Fed pauses in H1 2027.

headline: MINEROS FORMALISES $110M GOLD TREASURY — Borrowed $18.5M Against Bullion; Analyst Eyes Collateral Risk
snippet: Colombian gold producer Mineros S.A. has formalised a strategic gold reserve policy holding US$110 million of physical bullion in treasury, while also entering repurchase agreements that borrowed $18.5 million net cash against 5,100 ounces of gold — a structure analysts are flagging as a risk management challenge in a falling gold price environment. The company reported record H1 2026 revenue and profits but generated negative operating cash flow of $30.8 million due to the bullion accumulation programme. While Mineros's strategy reflects a broader trend of mid-tier producers treating their own metal as a balance sheet asset, repo-agreement exposure creates mark-to-market risk in a market where gold has fallen 7% in 20 sessions.
